docs.purpose: Returns the current data-quality dashboard and its 30-day trend: permit, trade, property and committee-of-adjustment metrics, detected volume, schema and duration anomalies, recent pipeline failures, and live database health statistics — for staff monitoring system health.
docs.data_story: It reads 4 tables — `data_quality_snapshots`, `pipeline_runs`, `logic_variables` and `pg_stat_user_tables` and writes nothing. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. It is called from 1 place: `admin_data_quality`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: No SPEC LINK file path — inline comments reference 'Spec 26 §3.4' by number only, so spec is left unmeasured per the hard rule. This route is classified PUBLIC by route-guard.ts despite serving internal health data; the engine-health query is deliberately scoped to a curated 11-table allowlist rather than all public tables to avoid disclosing row counts for sensitive tables, with a disclosure ruling filed pending in docs/reports/review_followups.md. pg_stat_user_tables is a Postgres catalog view, not an application table. Engine-health thresholds are read from seven logic_variables keys with a loud aggregated warning fallback to module defaults. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: DISCLOSURE (unauthenticated): an anonymous caller receives (a) the ENTIRE latest data_quality_snapshots row plus the last 30 days of them via SELECT * (src/lib/quality/metrics.ts:274) — that is the full operational-metrics surface: total_permits, active_permits, builders_with_phone/email/website, coa_* counts, null_* counts, violation_* counts, last_sync_at/last_sync_status, sla_permits_ingestion_hours, and schema_column_counts (a per-table COLUMN COUNT for permits/builders/coa_applications/parcels/permit_trades/permit_parcels — src/lib/quality/metrics.ts:642-647), i.e. schema-shape reconnaissance; (b) pipeline INTERNALS — pipeline names and, for any pipeline whose latest run failed, the raw `error_message` verbatim (route.ts:186-190), which can carry stack/SQL fragments; (c) live pg_stat_user_tables row counts, dead-tuple counts and scan counts for 11 named tables (route.ts:224-234). No per-user or per-permit PII. The file itself flags the boundary it did NOT cross: route.ts:198-208 records that widening the engine-health scope from 11 to all 87 tables would publish row counts for admin_backup_codes, admin_audit_log, subscribe_nonces, stripe_webhook_events, profiles, user_profiles and device_tokens, and says it is blocked on an auth ruling. That is a comment (a claim), but the CODE corroborates it: the ANY($1) list at route.ts:232-234 contains only the 11 business tables. The exposure of `error_message` and `schema_column_counts` is the part no comment defends. CHECKLIST agreement: routes-index.json census_reads (data_quality_snapshots, pipeline_runs, logic_variables, pg_stat_user_tables) matches exactly. The 7 logic_variables are Zod-bounded only for finiteness, never for range — a seeded 0 or a negative value would pass NumericVariableValue (route.ts:29-34) and silently disable an anomaly check. | Caching: none observed — no revalidate/dynamic export and no Cache-Control header in src/app/api/quality/route.ts:1-285 | Other guards / classification: PUBLIC: '/api/quality' is in PUBLIC_PREFIXES (src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:75), matched at route-guard.ts:170 -> 'public'; middleware pass-through src/middleware.ts:43-45. The file's own comments (route.ts:41-43, :204-205) state this and the code acts on it — the engine-health table list is deliberately curated to 11 tables (route.ts:232-234) rather than all 87. | Locking tests: src/tests/db/ledger-gate-callers.db.test.ts, src/tests/quality.infra.test.ts.
